# M0-1b: Per-category Jev confidence breakdown (offline, from cache)

- Milestone: M0
- Branch / worktree: `t/M0-1b`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M0-1b`
- Depends on: M0-1 (merged)
- Touches (exclusive while running): `spikes/jev/`, `docs/build/spikes/jev.md`
- Plan refs: none needed; read `docs/build/spikes/jev.md` (M0-1's findings)
- YNAB access: none. **Jev access: none.** Work only from the cache.
- Deploy: no

## Goal
Brendan is going to simplify the YNAB category list dramatically and wants to know which categories Jev struggled with
most. Produce a per-category breakdown from M0-1's cached answers, with **zero** API calls.

## Inputs
- The cache dir is `~/dev/github.com/deasa/YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/_data/jev-cache`, outside git. It holds `ynab.json`
  and `jev_<variant>_off<N>.json`. Pass it with `-cache`.
- The Jev call counter there is already at its 300 cap. Any code path that would call Jev must stay unreachable. Add an
  explicit `-offline` flag that fails instead of calling any API, and use it.

## Scope
- Add a per-category report to `spikes/jev` (offline mode). Focus on the recommended variant
  (`batch10+history+policy`, both off0 and off100, n≈200), and add a compact column for the bare `single` variant for
  contrast. For each **true** category:
  - n;
  - mean p_top when it's the true label;
  - top-1 accuracy;
  - the share that falls below τ=0.8;
  - its most common wrong pick.
- Also list the **predicted** categories with the lowest precision, and the most frequent confused pairs (true → predicted).
- Add a section "Per-category difficulty (for the category simplification)" to `docs/build/spikes/jev.md`:
  - the table, sorted hardest first, flagging categories with n<3 as low-sample;
  - 3–6 bullets on patterns, e.g. overlapping categories that should merge, or categories that need a description.

  Aggregates and category names only. No payees, amounts or dates.

## Out of scope
- Any API call (YNAB or Jev). New variants. Changing the τ recommendation. `docs/plan/*`, `CLAUDE.md`.

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] `go run . -cache <dir> -offline …` prints the per-category report. State that the Jev call counter in the cache is
      unchanged (still 300) after your runs.
- [ ] The new section exists in `docs/build/spikes/jev.md` with the sorted table and the pattern bullets.
- [ ] The branch diff contains no payee names, amounts, raw responses or ids (grep it and show the check).
- [ ] Root `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` still green.

## Result
- Status: DONE
- What changed:
  - `spikes/jev/main.go`: new `-offline` flag. The YNAB fetch is replaced by a cache-only fill that fails on a miss, and
    `jevClient.ask` returns an error before touching the counter or the network. New `-percat` flag (implies `-offline`)
    prints the report and exits.
  - `spikes/jev/percat.go`: `byTruth` (n, top-1, mean p_top, share below τ0.8, top wrong pick; hardest first), `byPrediction`
    (precision overall and at τ), `confusions` (true → predicted, with the count at ≥τ). Pools
    `batch10+history+policy` off0+off100 (n=200) with a `single` off0 contrast column.
  - `spikes/jev/percat_test.go`: unit tests for the three aggregations, plus a test that offline mode never calls Jev
    (calls stay 0).
  - `docs/build/spikes/jev.md`: new section "Per-category difficulty (for the category simplification)" with the sorted
    table (low-n flagged), the lowest-precision table, the confusion table and 6 pattern bullets.
- Acceptance:
  - `cd spikes/jev && go run . -cache ../../../_data/jev-cache -offline -percat` printed the report (exit 0). Jev
    counter `_data/jev-cache/jev_calls` was 300 before and 300 after every run, and its mtime was unchanged → **pass**.
  - The section exists in `docs/build/spikes/jev.md`, sorted hardest first, with the pattern bullets → **pass**.
  - Leak grep on the staged diff: 0 UUIDs, 0 `$<digit>` amounts, 0 ISO dates, 0 raw-response JSON keys. I matched all 170
    distinct cached payee strings (≥4 chars) against added lines, and every hit is a category name (e.g. "Subs - Canva",
    "Google One", "Highland City Utilities"), the YNAB product name, or the existing CLAUDE.md "Amazon orders" policy
    text → **pass**.
  - Root `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` is green. `spikes/jev` is its own module: `go vet . && go test ./...`
    there is green too → **pass**.
- Deviations from brief: "mean p_top when it's the true label" is computed as the mean p_top over all transactions whose
  true label is that category. The cache stores only p_top and top-3, not the probability of the true label, so that
  reading was the only one possible offline.
- Follow-ups for backlog: Decide, during the category simplification, whether purpose-based categories (Christmas, Tech
  Replacement, Generosity, Under The Radar, Next Trip) become manual-only via `EXCLUDED_CATEGORY_KEYWORDS`. Christmas
  misses were all at p_top ≥ 0.8. After the simplification, re-measure with a fresh Jev budget.
- Docs follow-ups: none (the spike doc was updated in this branch).
